stem: The Earth's interior is made up of how many main layers?
solution: The Earth has three layers: the crust (outermost), the mantle (middle) and the core (innermost).

stem: Which is the outermost layer of the Earth?
solution: The crust is the thin, outermost solid layer on which we live.

stem: The innermost and hottest layer of the Earth is the:
solution: The core is the innermost layer; its inner part is extremely hot and is made mainly of nickel and iron ('nife').

stem: The continental crust is composed mainly of silica and alumina, referred to as:
solution: The continental crust ('sial') is rich in silica (si) and alumina (al); the oceanic crust ('sima') is rich in silica and magnesium.

stem: The central core of the Earth is made up largely of which metals?
solution: The core is composed mainly of nickel (ni) and iron (fe), hence called 'nife'.

stem: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma are called:
solution: Igneous rocks form when hot molten magma/lava cools and hardens (e.g. basalt, granite).

stem: Rocks formed by the accumulation and compression of sediments over long periods are:
solution: Sedimentary rocks (e.g. sandstone) form from layers of sediment that get compacted and cemented over time.

stem: When existing rocks change form under great heat and pressure, the new rocks formed are called:
solution: Metamorphic rocks form when igneous or sedimentary rocks are transformed by intense heat and pressure (e.g. marble from limestone).

stem: The continuous process by which one type of rock changes into another over time is called the:
solution: The rock cycle describes how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks transform into one another over geological time.

stem: Naturally occurring substances with definite chemical composition, of which rocks are made, are called:
solution: Minerals are naturally occurring substances with a specific chemical composition; rocks are aggregates of one or more minerals.
